summary: Summit lookout on Mount St. Helens: 1916 house, cupola built 1918-1921, staffed into the 1920s, abandoned about 1929, all remains removed by the May 1980 eruption.

facts.design: Wooden house about 12 by 12 feet with a cupola (1916 newspaper plan); cupola later described as a D-6 type
facts.status_note: All remains removed by the May 1980 eruption; by 1980 the register says only the foundation was left
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Columbia National Forest in 1916); site now in Gifford Pinchot National Forest

events.note: Lookout erected on the summit per the July 9, 1916 newspaper report, which describes angle-iron construction; the July 20, 1916 report gives the planned wooden 12-foot house
Edward Robinson, patrolman at Spirit Lake, likely first staffed the site (WillhiteWeb)
Cupola construction began; work ran until 1921
Temporary employee John Walker died after a rockslide while repairing the telephone line to the lookout
Cupola work finished; HistoryLink gives 1918-1921 as the three-year build span
Glen H. Meissner reported 16 fires in one day; the newspaper and WillhiteWeb describe the Portland building differently
Family account (unverified): the writer's father is placed on the Spirit Lake district in 1927 and helped remove salvageable equipment during a summer assignment; the removal year is not stated
Abandoned about 1929; HistoryLink says the summit lookout was in use to 1929
May 1980 eruption permanently removed all remains

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Newspapers report a lookout house erected in summer 1916; the register and WillhiteWeb date cupola construction to 1918-1921, the same span HistoryLink gives. The story treats the 1916 house and the cupola as separate stages.

Most sources say abandoned about 1929 and HistoryLink says in use to 1929. A family account places the writer's father on the district in 1927 and says he helped remove salvageable equipment during a summer assignment, without dating the removal.
The register says only the foundation was left by 1980; WillhiteWeb says the foundation and a few remnants. Both agree the May 1980 eruption removed the rest.
The 1924 newspaper says the Portland fire struck stock show buildings; WillhiteWeb says a building in Portland. The story gives both wordings.

notes_for_editor: Search summaries attached a Mavie Olson 'Lady Lookout' staffing and a 1922 completion date to this site. HistoryLink ties Olson to the Finley Peak lookout in the Olympics and the 1922 completion to Mount Adams, so neither is used. The brief's record checks out (coordinates match FFLOS; 2012 registration confirmed); no corrections proposed. No source read describes access or the current condition of the summit, so access is omitted. The family account on the register page is unverified and is labelled as such in the story.
